hypotheses.idea: Delete writable DONE authority; derive CausalDone from canonical support.
Delete terminal receipt authority entirely; expose only reconstructible closure witnesses.
Factor terminality into OUTCOME_SETTLED, REENTRY_CLOSED and LEARNING_DECIDED instead of one monolithic DONE.
Represent completion as one typed support hyperedge spanning execution, episode/use, outcome, credit and delta/no-learning.
Use an append-only event-sourced closure predicate; current closure is a fold, not a mutable terminal row.
Use bitemporal terminal validity so later support invalidation can quarantine causal closure without erasing external outcome history.
Use a Merkle-like closure witness hash over exact support identities, recomputed on read.
Allow a fast DONE cache, but make it rebuildable/non-authoritative and bind it to a support epoch/hash.
Represent closure as a provenance expression whose derivation records exactly why completion holds.
Require a typed proof object to construct terminal projection; strings cannot satisfy the constructor.
Model effect->outcome->reentry as linear typestate/session progression; terminal value exists only after protocol completion.
Proof-carrying completion: terminal consumer validates a compact completion certificate against a fixed policy.
Monotone logic only: external outcome facts accumulate; non-monotone causal validity is queried separately, preventing terminal state conflation.
Keep ordinary persisted DONE but add canonical FKs/triggers plus atomic terminal transaction and read-time revalidation.

selection_reason: H1 directly attacks the newly reproduced failure class while remaining non-overlapping with active PR279/280 implementation ownership. H14 is retained as the strongest conventional baseline, not discarded.
